svg.text: Diagram 4 of 4 — Steady-state runtime + threat surface (every query)

Only the flows that happen once a cluster is RUNNING · runtime identity = Compute SA / Cluster SA; governed reads use vended UC SA tokens; the Workspace SA (launcher) does not appear on this view at all

g.text: User access
Control plane
Data plane (Google APIs)
Optional public egress
VPC-SC boundary
B# crossing

svg.text: PAS: no public access · IP lists
browser · REST / CLI · corp VPN route
IDENTITY · VMs run as Compute SA / Cluster SA · governed reads (F7–F9)
use vended UC storage-credential SA tokens — never the VM's own SA
firewall: egress to PSC 443 / 6666 / 8443–8451 · PGA for Google APIs
BQ API + Storage Read API · TLS 443
Boundary crossings — what a reviewer checks

g.text: B1 · Corp network → perimeter (frontend PSC)
Private DNS only — no public resolution · PAS: public_access_enabled =
false · private_access_level = ACCOUNT · IP access lists enforced
B2 · Frontend endpoint → plproxy attachment
Leaves the perimeter on a PSC private wire only — traffic never
touches the public internet (Google backbone end-to-end)
B3 · Backend endpoint → ngrok attachment (SCC)
Relay is cluster-initiated (outbound 6666) — no inbound path to the
cluster exists · relay never carries user traffic
B5 · Cluster → NAT → public internet (F10)
Optional — exists only for package installs · removable with private
mirrors, enabling a deny-all-egress posture
VPC-SC ingress · Cluster → protected buckets / BQ
identity = vended UC SA only · methods scoped (RO: objects.get /
list) · source-pinned to Databricks project numbers — the gate that
stops authenticated exfiltration to foreign buckets
F1 Analyst → frontend endpoint — TLS 443 · Okta session / PAT · B1
F4 Cluster → control plane REST · UC metadata · token issuance — 443¹
F5 Cluster → SCC relay — TCP 6666 · cluster-initiated · B3
F7 Cluster → GCS data lake — 443 via PGA · vended UC RO SA · gated
F8 Cluster → GCS analytics — 443 via PGA · vended UC RW SA · gated
F9 Cluster → BigQuery + Storage Read API — 443 · UC / connection SA
F10 Cluster → NAT → package repos — 443 · optional · B5
K KMS ↔ disks / workspace GCS / managed services — CMEK

svg.text: Identity plane — deliberately not drawn on the wires
Okta OIDC: browser ↔ Okta ↔ control plane (back-channel) — none of it
rides the analyst → frontend-PSC wire (F1) itself.
SCIM user/group sync: Okta → Account API (outside the perimeter).

¹ F4 routing verified against Databricks PSC docs: the workspace (plproxy) attachment serves both user access and cluster-originated REST / UC calls — the dp-<ws-id> DNS record resolves to the frontend endpoint IP; the ngrok relay carries only SCC on 6666 and never user traffic.
B4 (account plane → service project) and B6 (control plane → GCE API, as the Workspace SA) are setup / launch crossings — see diagrams 2 and 3. They do not occur on the steady-state query path.
